title: Paper 1 test-suite report and latency (SUT build A)
environment: the SUT's own project .venv (unlocked; read-only use; versions recorded in the run manifest); no lock is claimed

test_report.no_early_stop: no -x: every collected test runs; failures are reported, not fixed

latency.evaluator: in-process services.evaluator.app.evaluate(question, candidate_answer, get_rubric(qid)) on the 64 stored benchmark (question, answer, qid) triples in stored order, request i uses triple i mod 64; latency measurement only, scores are not used
latency.phases: (1) asset load (_ensure_evaluator_assets_loaded) timed once; (2) first request timed once (cold); (3) N=100 warm requests timed individually
latency.sqlite_write: N=100 sequential services.storage.database.save_attempt writes on one connection to a fresh temporary database (as in the frozen Paper 1 script, uncontended)
latency.statistics: raw per-request values stored; median, P95, P99 (numpy linear interpolation) with iid bootstrap 95% percentile CIs (B=10000, default_rng(42)); with N=100 the P99 is set by the largest two samples and is reported with that caveat
latency.no_sla: no SLA is defined; results are not labelled pass/fail

interpretation: only the stored, dated JUnit report and raw latency lists may be cited; a failing test is a finding; the scope of the latency numbers is one machine, one process, evaluation of stored benchmark answers, DB writes uncontended
